groups.title: React's virtual DOM and component model
groups.question: You are building a recipe page in React where a parent shows a list and a child shows details and a 'save' button. Explain how React decides what to update and how data moves between these components.

followUps.How React diffs the virtual DOM to minim: How does React avoid rebuilding the whole page on every state change?
followUps.Unidirectional data flow: props down, ca: How does the child tell the parent that 'save' was clicked?

evidence.text: React keeps a description of the UI and builds a new one on each render.
It compares the new description with the previous one.
Only the parts that changed are applied to the real DOM.

notEnough: Only saying React uses a virtual DOM.

evidence.text: Data flows from parent to child through props.
The parent passes a callback, and the child calls it to report events.
One-way flow makes it easy to trace where a change came from.

groups.title: useState, useEffect, and the hooks model
groups.question: A counter logs the old value right after you set it, and a chat component keeps receiving messages after it is closed. Explain how state updates and effects work in React.

followUps.Why state updates are asynchronous and b: Why does reading state right after calling the setter give the old value?
followUps.useEffect cleanup prevents memory leaks: What should an effect's cleanup do for a subscription or timer?

evidence.text: Setting state schedules a re-render; the new value is available in the next render.
Multiple updates in the same event are batched into one render.
Within one render, state is a fixed snapshot.
An effect can return a cleanup function.
React runs it before the effect re-runs and when the component unmounts.
Without cleanup, timers, subscriptions and requests keep running and cause leaks or updates to unmounted components.

notEnough: Only saying cleanup prevents memory leaks.

groups.title: Building components with Vite and React
groups.question: You are starting a new React app with Vite and need pages for a recipe list, a recipe detail and a settings area with its own sidebar. Explain how the tooling and routing work.

followUps.Vite dev server: HMR, fast cold starts,: Why does Vite's dev server start fast, and how is the production build different?
followUps.Client-side routing with React Router v6: How do nested routes and Outlet let pages share a layout?

evidence.text: In development Vite serves source files as native ES modules without bundling.
Hot module replacement updates only the changed module in the browser.
For production, Vite bundles and optimizes the code with Rollup.
Routes can be nested so child pages share a parent's layout.
The parent renders an Outlet where the matching child appears.
Link and useNavigate move between pages without a full reload.

notEnough: Only saying React Router handles routes.

groups.title: Fetching data in components
groups.question: Your recipe list fetches data in a component, and a filter component next to it also needs the selected category. Explain how you would fetch data and share state between them.

followUps.Data fetching pattern in useEffect with: What states does a component need when it fetches data in an effect, and how do you cancel the request?
followUps.Lifting state to the nearest common ance: Two sibling components need the same category value. Where should it live?

evidence.text: The component tracks loading, data and error in state.
An AbortController cancels the request when the component unmounts or the inputs change.
Libraries like React Query automate this pattern with caching.

notEnough: Only saying you fetch inside useEffect.

evidence.text: The state moves up to the closest common parent.
The parent passes the value down as props and an update function as a callback.
This keeps one source of truth for the value.

notEnough: Only saying to lift state up.
